sections.heading: Where Hecate helps
sections.translation:
Hecate gives powerful help to anyone she chooses.
In the public assembly, she makes whoever she favors stand out.
And when men arm themselves for war that destroys lives,
the goddess stands beside those she chooses,
ready to grant them victory and glory.
She sits beside respected kings as they give judgment.

She helps, too, when men compete in games:
the goddess stands beside them and lends her strength.
The winner, victorious through power and strength,
easily carries off a fine prize, full of joy,
and brings glory to his parents.
She is good at helping riders, too, whenever she chooses.

For those who work the gray, rough sea
and pray to Hecate and the thundering Earth-shaker,
the glorious goddess easily grants a great catch—
and easily takes it away when it is in sight,
if that is what she wants.

With Hermes, she is good at making livestock thrive in their pens.
Herds of cattle, great herds of goats,
and flocks of woolly sheep—if she wishes,
she makes a few grow into many, or many dwindle to a few.

So, though her mother had no other child,
Hecate holds honored privileges among all the immortal gods.
Zeus, the son of Cronus, made her the nurse of all the young
who, after her, opened their eyes to the light of far-seeing Dawn.
From the beginning she has cared for the young.
These are her honors.
sections.summary: Hecate can help people in public life, war, sports, fishing, and farming. She also cares for the young.

cards.label: Hecate
cards.general: A goddess with powers over many parts of life.
cards.here: She chooses whom to help and can give success or take it away.

cards.label: Public assembly
cards.general: A gathering where a community discusses public matters.
cards.here: Hecate can make a person stand out among the speakers and listeners.

cards.label: Earth-shaker
cards.general: A name for Poseidon, god of the sea and earthquakes.
cards.here: People fishing at sea pray to him along with Hecate.

cards.label: Hermes
cards.general: A god associated with travel, messages, and livestock.
cards.here: He and Hecate help herds and flocks grow.

cards.label: Zeus
cards.general: The son of Cronus who becomes ruler of the gods.
cards.here: He gives Hecate the task of caring for the young.

cards.label: Dawn
cards.general: Eos, the goddess who brings the morning light.
cards.here: Seeing Dawn's light means coming into the world alive.

sections.heading: Cronus swallows his children
sections.translation:
Rhea had glorious children with Cronus:
Hestia, Demeter, and Hera with her golden sandals;
mighty Hades, whose heart knows no pity,
who lives in halls beneath the earth;
the thundering Earth-shaker, Poseidon;
and Zeus, wise in planning, father of gods and humans,
whose thunder makes the wide earth shake.

Great Cronus swallowed his children, each one
as it came from its mother's sacred womb to her knees.
He meant to keep any other glorious descendant of Uranus
from holding the royal honor among the immortal gods.
For he had learned from Gaia and starry Uranus
that he was destined, strong as he was,
to be overcome by his own son,
through the plans of great Zeus.

So Cronus kept watch with his eyes wide open,
and swallowed his own children as he waited for them.
Rhea was gripped by grief that would not fade.
sections.summary: Cronus learns that his son will overthrow him. He swallows his children as they are born, leaving Rhea in lasting grief.

cards.label: Rhea
cards.general: A daughter of Gaia and Uranus, and Cronus's partner.
cards.here: She is the mother of the six gods named in this passage.

cards.label: Cronus
cards.general: A son of Gaia and Uranus who rules the gods before Zeus.
cards.here: He swallows his children to prevent one of them from taking his power.

cards.label: Hestia
cards.general: The goddess of the hearth, the fire at the center of a home.
cards.here: She is one of Rhea and Cronus's daughters.

cards.label: Demeter
cards.general: A goddess of grain and farming.
cards.here: She is one of Rhea and Cronus's daughters.

cards.label: Hera
cards.general: A goddess of marriage who becomes queen of the gods.
cards.here: She is a daughter of Rhea and Cronus, pictured wearing golden sandals.

cards.label: Hades
cards.general: The god who rules the world of the dead beneath the earth.
cards.here: His underground home and pitiless heart mark his stern power.

cards.label: Poseidon
cards.general: The god of the sea and earthquakes, also called Earth-shaker.
cards.here: He is one of Rhea and Cronus's sons.

cards.label: Zeus
cards.general: The god of thunder who becomes ruler of the gods.
cards.here: He is the son whose plans will bring about Cronus's defeat. “Father of gods and humans” is a title of authority.

cards.label: Gaia
cards.general: Earth herself, a goddess and the mother of Cronus and Rhea.
cards.here: She tells Cronus that his own son will overcome him.

cards.label: Uranus
cards.general: Sky himself, a god and the father of Cronus and Rhea.
cards.here: He and Gaia reveal Cronus's fate. Cronus's children are also his descendants.

sections.heading: Rhea hides Zeus
sections.translation:
But when Rhea was about to give birth to Zeus,
father of gods and humans,
she begged her own dear parents,
Gaia and starry Uranus, to help her devise a plan:
to give birth to her dear child in secret,
and to win revenge for her father
and for the children great Cronus, with his crooked schemes,
had swallowed.

They listened closely to their dear daughter and agreed to help.
They told her all that fate had in store
for King Cronus and his strong-hearted son.
They sent her to Lyctus, in the fertile land of Crete,
when she was about to bear her youngest child,
great Zeus. Vast Gaia received him from her
to nourish and care for him on the broad island of Crete.

Through the swift, black night Rhea carried him,
coming first to Lyctus.
Taking him in her arms, she hid him
in a deep cave, in the hidden places of the holy earth,
on Mount Aegeum, thick with forest.
sections.summary: Rhea asks her parents to help save her next baby. She gives birth to Zeus on Crete, where he is hidden in a cave.

cards.label: Rhea
cards.general: Cronus's partner and the mother of his children.
cards.here: She seeks a way to save her youngest child, Zeus.

cards.label: Gaia and Uranus
cards.general: Earth and Sky, the parents of Rhea and Cronus.
cards.here: They help Rhea plan Zeus's secret birth, and Gaia receives him into her care.

cards.label: Cronus
cards.general: The ruler of the gods before Zeus.
cards.here: Rhea seeks revenge for his swallowing their children and for his earlier attack on his father, Uranus.

cards.label: Zeus
cards.general: The youngest child of Rhea and Cronus, destined to rule the gods.
cards.here: His mother hides him so Cronus cannot swallow him.

cards.label: Lyctus
cards.general: An ancient town on Crete, a large Greek island.
cards.here: Rhea's parents send her there for Zeus's birth.

cards.label: Mount Aegeum
cards.general: The mountain on Crete named here as Zeus's hiding place.
cards.here: Its thick forest and deep cave shelter the baby.

uncertainties: In lines 471–473, the Greek leaves the subject of the revenge clause unstated. The translation takes Rhea as seeking revenge for Uranus and her swallowed children; the clause can also be understood as referring to Zeus taking that revenge.
In lines 481–483, the Greek does not name the female figure who carries and hides Zeus. The translation follows the reading that this is Rhea; Gaia is also possible.
The exact location of Mount Aegeum is uncertain.
